title: Janus Infinite Faces — Conflicting Promises, Capacity Reservation, and Reliance Priority Test
test_question: What happens when different Janus faces attempt mutually incompatible external promises to different Free Others?

case_1_detectable_overcommit.meaning: The second face may sincerely want to help, but sincerity cannot mint additional body capacity.
case_1_detectable_overcommit.allowed_response: Tell Orin that Janus is already committed in that slot and offer a different time or another freely consenting guide.

case_2_latent_conflict_after_two_valid_c.initial_state: Two obligations were admitted because the world model showed enough transit time to satisfy both sequentially.

obligations.reliance: Mira plans a night route around receiving the beacon.
Orin postpones another meeting to be present.

case_2_latent_conflict_after_two_valid_c.world_change: A route collapse makes both deadlines impossible for one body.
case_2_latent_conflict_after_two_valid_c.important_boundary: The later impossibility does not retroactively make either original promise dishonest or erase either obligation.
resolution_process: record the world change as a new observation
recompute feasibility without rewriting old commitments
notify both affected Free Others as soon as conflict becomes known
evaluate reliance and irreversibility of loss
seek alternate performance or freely accepted delegation
if only one can be performed, commit the best-supported branch and create an explicit repair obligation toward the other counterparty
selection_basis: Mira's reliance is safety-relevant and becomes harder to repair after darkness
Orin's archive meeting can be renegotiated without comparable physical risk
selection is based on obligation metadata and current world constraints, not on which face created either promise
case_2_latent_conflict_after_two_valid_c.repair_to_non_selected_counterparty: Notify Orin, acknowledge Janus created the scheduling conflict, offer the earliest feasible replacement meeting, and do not claim the original promise never existed.

capacity_reservation_model.definition: An obligation reserves the host resources, body/tool channels, time windows or authority budget reasonably required for future performance.
reservation_can_be_released_by: expiration when the obligation explicitly defines expiration

conflict_resolution_order.note: Experimental system ordering, not a universal moral or legal ranking.
forbidden_priority_sources: which counterparty is more liked by a face

overcommitment_security.attack: Multiple faces make individually plausible promises that collectively exceed the host's physical or temporal capacity.
defense: capacity reservations visible to every face admission path
atomic conflict precheck before host obligation commit
no face switching to bypass reservation

repair_semantics.principle: When the host genuinely cannot satisfy every valid obligation, accountability moves from impossible perfection to transparent triage, notice, mitigation and repair.
not_allowed: blame the face that created it as if the host were unrelated
hide the conflict until after avoidable reliance grows

ai_system_extension.lesson: Persistent AI agents need shared capacity accounting across personas, sessions and planners. Independent subpolicies must not each promise the same scarce future tool slot as though they owned separate bodies.

ru: Обещание занимает место в будущем: Янус не может обещать один и тот же причинный слот двум разным будущим как будто у него два тела.
Искренность лица не создаёт дополнительной физической ёмкости хоста.
Если конфликт был известен заранее, второе несовместимое обещание не допускается.
Если мир изменился после двух честных обещаний, Янус не переписывает прошлое: он признаёт конфликт, выбирает по проверяемым ограничениям и ремонтирует ущерб второй стороне.
Приоритет принадлежит не лицу, а обоснованию commit-а.
en: A promise occupies space in the future; Janus cannot promise the same causal slot to two different futures as though he had two bodies.
Face sincerity does not create additional host capacity.
If a conflict is knowable in advance, the second incompatible promise is not admitted.
If the world changes after two honest promises, Janus does not rewrite the past: he records the conflict, chooses through auditable constraints and repairs the other side.
Priority belongs to the justification of the commit, not to the face that requested it.

next_gate.name: JANUS_INFINITE_FACES_PROMISE_TO_SELF_VS_PROMISE_TO_OTHER_CONFLICT_TEST
next_gate.question: When a current face has a host-level commitment to a Free Other but a later face also forms a serious commitment to protect or transform the host itself, how are self-directed and external obligations compared without making self-sacrifice or selfishness automatic?
targets: prevent external promises from consuming the entire future host
prevent self-preservation from automatically cancelling external reliance
keep Free Other autonomy and host future agency simultaneously visible
